prompt: Implement the Composite pattern: FolderEntry holds leaf FileEntry objects and other folders, and totalSize, fileCount and depth must all work recursively at any nesting level.
explanation: Composite works because leaves and containers share one type -- Entry -- so a folder can treat every child the same way. totalSize() just adds up child.totalSize(); when the child is another folder that call recurses, and when it is a file it simply returns the file's size. fileCount() and depth() need instanceof to tell leaves from sub-folders, since only folders can contain more entries.
hints: add should call children.add(child) and then return this, which is what makes chained calls work.
totalSize() never needs to know what kind of child it has: calling child.totalSize() does the right thing for both files and folders.
For depth(), track the largest depth() among the sub-folders and return 1 + that, which is 1 when there are no sub-folders.
